$comment: THE committed exclusion list of specs/sor-site/surface/spec.md — one fact, one file. Consumed by BOTH tiers: tests/test_surface_contract.py (A2, source scan over shipped .ts/.tsx/.js/.css) and e2e/tests/static.spec.ts (B7, scan over built JS bundles). A pattern written as a bare string runs in both tiers, word-boundary and case-sensitive as written; an object entry narrows to one tier ('source' | 'bundle') and records why in its 'why'. The two files previously carried two hand-maintained copies and had diverged at birth (found 2026-08-13); do not add a pattern to one tier's consumer directly — add it here.

carveOuts.$comment: Spec A2: 'ReadingProgress carved out of any progress pattern' — the local scroll indicator is a kept content primitive. Both tiers scrub every occurrence of these tokens from the text before any pattern runs.

brand.$comment: De-brand (settled lead decision 2026-08-13): no upstream brand strings in shipped source or built output; branding comes from the consuming site's config. Case-insensitive so AgentFactory/agent-factory/AGENT_FACTORY cannot slip past a case-exact scan.

scaffoldMarkdown.$comment: The MARKDOWN tier, added 2026-08-14 (tests/test_surface_contract.py). The .ts/.tsx/.js/.css tiers above never read a word of prose, yet 12 SKILL.md files and 4 rules crossed into the scaffold from an ~80-skill CURRICULUM repo — the one place where brand and lesson vocabulary is most likely to survive, and the only thing holding the line was review. Scans packages/vsor/src/vsor/templates/scaffold/**/*.{md,json} with the brand pattern above plus the curriculum pattern here. The spec's A2 clause already recorded the one carve-out below as an exception; this is the scan it was an exception to.
scaffoldMarkdown.curriculumWhy: The words a tax-law or medical SoR must never find in its own scaffold. `teach`/`teaching` are deliberately absent: they are ordinary English here ('an unmaintained skill teaching a moving target'), and a pattern that cries wolf gets deleted. 'of course' is excluded by lookbehind for the same reason — technical-clarity's minimiser list names it as a word to avoid, which is content, not branding.

brandCarveOuts.why: the framework's own repository URL — a factual pointer, verified against `git remote -v`, not corpus branding. Named as an exception in specs/sor-site/surface/spec.md's A2 clause. The line is exempted, not the file.

@docusaurus/theme-common bundles its blog-authors class-name table even with the blog preset off; the excluded authors DATA cannot reach a bundle without its source first failing this row's source tier or the path scan

Docusaurus itself serializes a customFields key (empty here) into every site bundle, so a bundle string scan cannot distinguish product endpoints from the framework default; the 12 endpoint exclusion is enforced by this source tier plus the A1 allowlist

rows.$comment: Added 2026-08-14, closing the list against the spec table (it had 10 of the 12 rows since birth). The five duplicate tab plugins collapsed into lib/remark-tabs BEFORE crossing; the app components they wrapped did not cross at all. The names had survived in remark-tabs' own doc comments as examples of what a consuming site would write — scrubbed in the same change, which is why this row is green rather than carved out. The kebab alternates were added 2026-08-14 (second pass): the patterns are case-sensitive, so an excluded component that crossed in its CLASS-NAME form went unseen by both tiers — 45 lines of `.tool-tabs` styling had reached every built stylesheet. `os-tabs` is deliberately NOT listed: unlike the other three it is a live directive name this framework itself emits (lib/remark-tabs/presets.js osTabs, registered in the shell's own config), so it is vocabulary that crossed, not a component that did not. `OSTabs`, the component, stays excluded.
Added 2026-08-14 with the row above. LocaleDropdown and RomanUrdu are filed under 'Translated content' below, where the spec table also places the i18n half of this row.

patterns.why: the excluded upstream directory, as a path segment; the bundle tier would match any minified string containing 'translation/' from a dependency's own i18n plumbing
